title: Bug Report Studio — From Messy Notes to a Clear Report
description: Paste a messy bug description and a heuristic parser pulls out imperative repro steps, expected and actual results, the app version and a draft title; then refine it with a title helper, environment details read locally from your own browser, drag-to-reorder steps, a severity × priority matrix with guidance, and simulated log attachments. A report-quality score explains exactly what is missing, and the finished report exports as Markdown.
prompt: Build 'Bug Report Studio'. I paste a messy bug description — the kind you get in chat — and it helps me turn it into a structured report: a title helper (where / what goes wrong / when), environment capture that reads the real navigator and screen info but only shows it locally with a way to exclude rows, numbered repro steps with drag reorder (and a keyboard way), expected vs actual, a severity × priority matrix with guidance on what each combination means and when a mismatch needs justifying, an attachments list with simulated console and network snippets from a fictional app, and a report-quality score with specific suggestions for what to fix next. Export as Markdown. Save the draft in localStorage. Make it look like a naturalist's field notebook — specimen plate, serif headings, moss and rust.

methodology: Golden-input parsing: the built-in messy example is a fixed input, so the spec asserts the exact five imperative steps, expected/actual sentences, version string and composed title the heuristic must produce.

Score arithmetic as an oracle: each rule has a fixed weight, so a structured example must score exactly 80 (title 25 + steps 25 + results 25 + version 5) and adding environment, triage and evidence must reach exactly 100.
Environment values checked against the test's own viewport (page.viewportSize), so the same assertion holds on desktop and Pixel 7 without branching.
Three reorder routes for steps — Alt+Arrow keys, move buttons, and a pointer drag on the grip — each verified by the resulting order and the Markdown numbering.
Roving-focus radiogroup for the matrix: click plus arrow-key navigation, aria-checked and focus asserted, and guidance text checked for consistent and mismatched combinations.
Persistence: after a reload the steps, triage cell and score are restored from localStorage (saved synchronously on every change).
risks: The parser is heuristic: new phrasing in the messy text (other verbs, no punctuation) can yield fewer steps — the status message tells users to review every field.
Drag reordering by moving DOM nodes during the gesture can lose pointer capture; capture is held on the stable list element instead of the moving row.
User-agent parsing for the browser name drifting as UA strings change (the full UA is always included as a fallback).
qa.playwright: Most of the page is deterministic text transformation, which suits exact-value assertions (toHaveValue, toEqual on an evaluateAll of the step inputs) better than screenshots. The environment panel reads live browser properties, so instead of hard-coding values the test derives expectations from page.viewportSize() and only checks stable facts like 'Chrome'. The drag test uses page.mouse down/move/up with intermediate steps over the grip; Chromium delivers these as pointer events on both the desktop and touch-emulated mobile projects. The Blob download is verified through its status message, and tests never clear localStorage mid-run — each test gets a fresh context — which avoids racing the autosave.
coverage: Messy example parsed into exact steps, results, version and title; score 80
Title flags for short, vague and shouty titles; compose from helper
Step reorder via Alt+Arrow, move button, pointer drag; delete
Environment capture matches the viewport; excluded rows leave the Markdown
Matrix click and arrow keys with guidance; attachments; score 100; download; reload persistence

a11y: Every input is labelled, steps have named move/delete buttons plus Alt+Arrow reordering so dragging is never required, and the severity × priority matrix is a roving-tabindex radiogroup with named cells. The parse result, title flags, guidance and grade are announced through live regions.
